newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia offered to defend baht, says Thai minister.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia offered to defend baht, says Thai minister.

text.p: Malaysia offered to defend the baht during a recent speculative attack on the Thai currency, Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan revealed on Friday.
"There have been offers from countries (of the region), including Malaysia, but we have not used the facilities," he told a news conference.
Malaysia's central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, has not commented on whether the Thai government had sought its help to defend the baht during a sharp attack on the currency in mid-May.
But the Monetary Authority of Singapore said it intervened in the market, along with the Bank of Thailand, to help the baht during the recent assault on the currency.
Central banks in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have an ongoing pact to defend each other's currrencies in times of such crises.
"There has been some manipulation, some attack on our currency," said Amnuay, visiting Kuala Lumpur on the invitation of Malaysia's acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
"The situation has calmed down and stabilised," he said.
Amnuay said Malaysia had gone through a similar currency turmoil in 1993 and "we can learn from experiences of Malaysia".
Since the assault on its currency, Thailand has introduced capital controls which have decreased foreign investors' access to the baht.
But Amnuay declined to give any details of the situation or how long the controls, under which overseas currency swaps have been stopped, will remain in place.
"It is not the place or time to discuss our plans," he said when asked if the country would formalise an exchange policy with other countries in the region.
